Hi Elena — thanks for the note and congrats on the conversion. Short answers up front, details below:

1) Proration: we can issue a prorated invoice for the remainder of the billing cycle (charge = daily rate * remaining days). Alternatively we can post a credit equal to the prorated amount to be applied against your next invoice — whichever you prefer.

2) Invoicing to parent & VAT: yes, we can invoice Lumino Holdings Ltd and consider reverse-charge only if you provide a valid EU VAT number (and certificate). If the parent is outside the EU and you have an EU-registered subsidiary that used the service, we need the VAT registration that applies to the billed entity.

3) Docs we need: legal entity name exactly as on VAT registry, VAT ID (pdf screenshot or certificate), purchase order number (if you want net-30). Once we have those we will:
   - reissue a prorated proforma showing the partial-period charge and tax treatment
   - either create a separate one-off invoice dated 2026-10-21 or apply a manual credit to next invoice (indicate which you prefer)

I attached a quick proforma estimate for the partial period (file: 20261020-proforma_estimate.pdf) with the prorate math used. For transparency: prorated_charge = (addon_monthly_cost / days_in_cycle) * remaining_days. In your case the addon monthly cost is quoted $9,000/mo; cycle runs 1st–30th; add-on started 19th so remaining days = 12 -> prorated = (9000/30)*12 = $3,600. Local VAT treatment will adjust the final invoice if VAT applies.

Next steps: if you want us to invoice Lumino Holdings Ltd, please send the VAT ID and PO number; if you'd rather have a credit applied, confirm and we'll post it and send an accounting note.

- Payment collection: Lumino asked for net-30 most likely; confirm payment method (ACH preferred for EU entity via SEPA). If card was used for initial charge, we should avoid refunds; prefer issuing a charge/line to parent and offset the original charge with an internal credit memo.
